solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sexism in the workplace?

parts.note: the whole clue playfully describes jobs being handed out only to men, the idiom for favouritism read literally as a male-only hiring policy

explanation.surface: A question about discrimination against women at work.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom normally means jobs given to friends and cronies; the clue reads 'boys' literally as males, turning it into sex discrimination.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes posts handed to insiders; taken literally, posts reserved for men is workplace sexism.

clue.text: Book two boys who got the British Standard remedy

parts.note: Jude is a boy's name
Theo is a second boy's name
BS is the abbreviation for British Standard, the UK specification mark
a remedy is a cure

explanation.surface: A story of two lads who were given an officially approved treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy's novel of 1895, so a book by title.

clue.text: Cheers dance that involves utmost movement

indicators.note: the dance word wraps around the other letters, so it involves them

parts.note: to bop is to dance, and a bop is a dance

indicators.note: the letters of utmost are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A toast at a dance where everyone moves energetically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' reads like part of the dance scene but is the anagram signal; 'involves' means the dance word wraps the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking toast, said when raising glasses, just as one might say cheers.

clue.text: Out after the first three, we're told

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard spoken, not seen written

parts.note: what comes after the first three in a sequence is the fourth

explanation.surface: Someone eliminated once the first three have gone, so they hear.
explanation.definitionFit: To go forth is to go out, as in setting forth from home.

clue.text: Others seek treatments offered by sanatoriums

parts.note: the rest means the others
cures are treatments for illness

explanation.surface: Other people go looking for therapies available at sanatoriums.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamilton lets 'treatments' do double duty: it supplies the second word and also reads into the definition of what sanatoriums offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Long periods of enforced rest were the classic regime prescribed in sanatoriums for invalids and nervous patients.

clue.text: See 1
Respite from endless traffic with chief engineer

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter, so it has no end

parts.note: to have truck with is to have dealings or traffic with

indicators.note: the chief, or leading, letter of the word engineer is taken

explanation.surface: A break from never-ending traffic, accompanied by the senior engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops K from TRUCK, an old word for dealings or trade; 'chief' takes only the first letter of engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is a temporary halt to fighting, a respite from hostilities.

clue.text: Contrariwise, teaching brings in new workers to start joining up

indicators.note: the reversed word takes another letter inside it
the word is turned the opposite way, read back to front

parts.note: lore is traditional teaching or knowledge
men can mean workers, as in a firm's men

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word to is taken

explanation.surface: Teaching admits new staff so they begin by signing on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrariwise' turns LORE into EROL; 'brings in' puts N inside it to give ENROL.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing on as a member or recruit is enlistment, the act of joining up.

clue.text: No taste in petticoats that are made to measure

indicators.note: the remaining letters are made into something new, rearranged

parts.note: the letters of petticoats form the pool
the letters of taste are the ones taken away from that pool

explanation.surface: Tailored petticoats lacking any taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No taste in petticoats' strips T, A, S, T, E from PETTICOATS, leaving P, T, I, C, O, which 'made' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: In British pubs an optic is the device fitted to an upturned spirits bottle that dispenses a fixed measure.

clue.text: Was a mess: sighed "please formulate an exercise regime"

indicators.note: to formulate is to put together in a new form, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A frazzled person sighs and asks someone to devise a fitness plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A system of kneading and stroking the muscles, a regime of bodily manipulation loosely called exercise.

clue.text: Make your mind up; mine is not to intimidate

indicators.note: the word mine is not there, so it is removed

parts.note: to determine is to make up your mind
taken as written

explanation.surface: Telling someone to decide, while declaring it is not one's place to bully.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter is to discourage by threat or fear, a synonym of intimidate.

clue.text: Abigail's mixing stout and beer

definitions.note: read as Abigail is; abigail is an old word for a lady's maid

indicators.note: the letters of the two drinks are mixed together into a new order

explanation.surface: Abigail is blending two kinds of beer in a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abigail's' means 'Abigail is', the 's being the link; an abigail, from a maid in a 17th-century play, is a lady's maid.
explanation.definitionFit: A soubrette is the pert maidservant role of comedy, and an abigail is likewise a lady's maid.

clue.text: Furthermore, facial hair disguises husband's affliction

parts.note: too means furthermore or also

indicators.note: the moustache hides the other letter inside it

parts.note: tache is short for moustache

explanation.surface: A moustache conceals a husband's ailment, as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A pain in the teeth is an ailment, a minor affliction.

clue.text: Fruit that gives a large number life force

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals, a fairly large number
chi, or qi, is the vital energy of Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: A fruit said to supply huge amounts of vitality.
explanation.definitionFit: A variant spelling of lychee, the sweet Chinese fruit.

clue.text: Follow directions around university

indicators.note: the compass letters go round the other letter

parts.note: E, N, S, E are compass directions east, north, south, east

explanation.surface: Instructions for finding the way around a campus.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to happen afterwards, to follow as a result.

clue.text: Come out with Charlie in US city in crisis

parts.note: to emerge is to come out

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York
Charlie is C in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone appears alongside Charlie in an American city during a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a sudden dangerous situation, a crisis needing urgent action.

clue.text: Element that's literally thin on the ground!

parts.note: rare air is thin air
earth is the ground

explanation.surface: A substance that is, quite literally, scarce in the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' points out that the phrase 'thin on the ground' spells the name when taken word for word.
explanation.definitionFit: The lanthanides such as cerium are a family of chemical elements known by this name.

clue.text: Laid off and turned out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Made jobless and thrown out on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like a second definition, but 'out' rearranges the letters of AND and TURNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers dismissed because their posts are cut are described as surplus to requirements.

clue.text: Imaginary place where girl goes after sport and bible class

indicators.note: the girl's name comes after the other pieces

parts.note: RU is rugby union
RI is religious instruction, the old British school subject
Tania is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Where a girl heads after games and scripture lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was the name for religious education lessons in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional central European kingdom of Anthony Hope's The Prisoner of Zenda.

clue.text: Work is forced upon subject

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
pressed means forced or pushed

explanation.surface: A job is imposed on a citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject people are under domination, kept down by those in power.

clue.text: See 1
This half weird humming sound

indicators.note: only the first two of this word's four letters are used

parts.note: rum is an old British word for strange or odd

explanation.surface: Something half-strange about a droning noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrum is a steady drone, a continuous low humming.

clue.text: See 8
IT set-up in the outskirts of Spalding generating gobbledegook

indicators.note: the network letters sit inside the town's outer letters
only the outer letters of the town's name are taken

parts.note: a LAN, local area network, is a computer network set-up

explanation.surface: A computer installation on the edge of Spalding, a Lincolnshire market town, producing nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal jargon that can sound like gibberish to outsiders.

clue.text: Walk with Mark in part of Italy, heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters run upwards, back to front
the letter goes inside the island's name

parts.note: Elba is an Italian island

explanation.surface: A stroll with Mark through part of Italy, going north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside ELBA to make ELMBA, which 'heading north' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow relaxed pace.

clue.text: I'm no sloth when travelling to Stonehenge, say

indicators.note: the letters travel around into a new order

explanation.surface: An energetic tourist insists they are no slouch on the trip to Stonehenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonehenge is made of great standing stones, examples of single huge stone blocks.

clue.text: Credit La Manche, say, for having it

parts.note: La Manche is the French name for the English Channel, a sea, and mer is French for sea
taken as written

explanation.surface: Praise for the English Channel, oddly, for having something.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth deserving praise, as in giving someone credit.

clue.text: Told to put down the machine

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to put down is to lay, followed by the word the

explanation.surface: Instructed to set down the device.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine tool that turns material against a cutter.

clue.text: Town centre is an almost civilised neighbourhood

indicators.note: the word stops one letter short

parts.note: urbane means refined or civilised
an area is a neighbourhood

explanation.surface: Claim that the middle of town is a nearly refined district.
explanation.definitionFit: A built-up district of a town, the opposite of countryside; loosely the town's heart.

clue.text: Where one might go from Southampton Gateway

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A destination reached by sailing from the Southampton port gateway.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pacific island kingdom, somewhere a traveller could visit as a destination.

clue.text: Caller who may be about to provoke a siege mentality?

definitions.text: Caller who may be about to provoke a siege mentality?

parts.words: Caller who may be about to provoke a siege mentality?
parts.note: a hostile visitor at the entrance could be a besieging army, which would understandably make those inside feel under siege

explanation.surface: A doorstep visitor who leaves the household feeling besieged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caller' suggests a friendly visitor, but here it is an attacking force outside the walls.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe outside the city walls is the literal besieger, so a defensive mindset follows.
